svg.text: THE SEND PATH — seven steps, one lock
typed ids ⇒ you cannot swap chatId and senderId by accident
server-side, never trusted from the client · blocked-user check is MISSING here
3 required + 4 optional fields ⇒ Builder, not a 7-arg constructor
chat.addMessage(m) — synchronized on the CHAT OBJECT
per-chat monitor ⇒ full parallelism ACROSS chats, safety WITHIN one
this is the one line the whole design is built to protect
messages.put(m.getId(), m) — the SAME object, not a copy
so star / delete / receipt by messageId are O(1) and stay visible in the chat list
addMessage marks the message delivered to the OTHER party
honest: there is no transport — "delivered" means the server accepted it
an Observer on addMessage would push to a WebSocket per device,
and queue for offline users. Named, not built — no subscriber in scope.
device has it · two grey ticks
updateOverallStatus() — three lines, no State pattern
this rolls up on ANY reader; real WhatsApp's blue tick is EVERY reader
one-line change (readBy ⊇ participants − sender) — confirm it, don't guess it
A group message isn't "delivered" — it is delivered TO BOB
and read BY CAROL. Two booleans cannot express that.
markDelivered / markRead are synchronized: each does a map
put PLUS an updateOverallStatus() recompute — compound.
the maps are the truth; status is a convenience for the tick UI ✓
unread count = messages after the per-user lastReadAt watermark,
O(messages since watermark) instead of a counter that drifts
THE TWO RACES THIS DESIGN CLOSES
BEFORE: check-then-act — search for a chat, create if absent.
Two callers both search, both miss, both create.
32 threads on the same pair → distinct chats: 32, 10, 11, 11, 6
FIX — a canonical key plus an atomic claim:
if (winner != null) return winner; // lost the race — drop our candidate
The loser's candidate was never published to any index — nothing to clean up.
The key is SORTED, so (a,b) and (b,a) must collide.
Bonus: replaced an O(chats-per-user) scan with an O(1) lookup ✓
The service was labelled "thread-safe using ConcurrentHashMap".
The registries were. The per-chat message list was a bare ArrayList.
Two threads read the same size, both write index n, one overwrites.
FIX — make the chat object its own monitor:
public synchronized List<Message> getMessages() { return copy; }
Cost: sends into ONE very busy group serialize. That's the right trade —
the answer to a hot group is a single-writer append log, not finer locks.
resolve chat → authorize sender → build immutable core → append under the chat's monitor → index by id → receipts accumulate per participant → status is derived, never set directly

g.text: Invariants defended: no lost messages · exactly one direct chat per pair · per-chat parallelism
Honest gaps: no transport · typing set has no TTL · blocked users not enforced on send · unbounded history
